newhire_anya: Hi team  first day QA engineer here. Pulled the repo and tried the devcontainer flow but my container can't ssh into our test VM (permission denied). Also my dotfiles haven't been wired up yet. Any quick checklist for ssh keys, direnv, and the container setup? Do I need to add keys to the host keychain or inside the container?

marc: welcome! For devcontainers we usually forward your ssh agent into the container instead of copying keys. In VS Code Remote - Containers enable 'Forward Agent'. On Mac, ensure your key is loaded: `ssh-add -l` to list, `ssh-add --apple-use-keychain ~/.ssh/id_ed25519` to add.

devx_elaine: +1. Checklist I run: 1) `git config --global user.email "anya@redwood.com"` & name, 2) confirm `~/.ssh/id_ed25519` perms `chmod 600`, 3) `direnv allow` after cloning (we use .envrc in a few services), 4) VS Code: Remote-Containers > Rebuild with SSH agent.

infra-bot: Onboarding snippets: <internal/dev-setup/ssh-agent-devcontainer.md> and <internal/dev-setup/direnv-and-envrc.md>. Remember: do not put secrets in dotfiles; use 1Password CLI for access tokens.

ops_ryan: If you see "Permission denied (publickey)", run `ssh -v git@internal-git` from both host and inside container to compare keys being offered. If nothing is offered inside container it's an agent-forwarding issue. Also macOS Ventura changed some keychain flags; if `ssh-add` complains try `--apple-use-keychain` (newer OpenSSH).

newhire_anya: thanks, forwarding sounds right. Quick question about dotfiles: should I symlink dotfiles into the container workspace or let the repo's .devcontainer copy them? I have zsh config and a small ~/.extra.env that exports API_TEST_DOMAIN.

marc: we prefer minimal host dotfiles inside container to avoid leaking personal config. Repo has `devcontainer/dotfiles-setup.sh` to selectively apply company starter configs. For env vars, put test-only overrides in `.env.test` and add to .gitignore; don't export secrets.

devx_elaine: also watch out for direnv + devcontainer: direnv runs in container shell if present. Ensure `direnv` is installed in the container image (our devcontainer image includes it). If you use zsh, put `eval "$(direnv export zsh)"` in your shell rc.

newhire_anya: tried agent-forwarding and `ssh-add -l` inside container shows my key  progress! One more: how do I get 1Password CLI available in the container to fetch test tokens?

ops_ryan: we mount 1password socket into container for interactive use; see `devcontainer.json` mounts. Alternatively use `op signin --session <token>` but we prefer socket mount so you still use local auth. Check `devcontainer/readme.md` for exact mount snippet.

devx_elaine: if anything breaks, paste outputs: `ssh -v git@internal-git`, `ssh-add -l`, `echo $SHELL`, `ls -la ~/.ssh`, and the small excerpt of your `devcontainer.json`. We can triage quickly.

newhire_anya: posting those now after I reprovision. Thanks everyone 389 :)
